network_thesis.headline: The region's largest ferry operator adds the foiling premium tier above its own fleet.
network_thesis.body: Hornblower Group (through its City Experiences portfolio) operates NYC Ferry, the harbor's largest public ferry system, alongside the National Park Service's Statue of Liberty/Ellis Island concession and City Cruises' dining and sightseeing product at Pier 15. The company is already mid-electrification of its own conventional hulls in this harbor. Navier adds a faster, foiling, premium-priced tier under the same crews, the same USCG-compliant operating practice, and the same docks — a product Hornblower runs itself, sold and priced apart from its subsidized public-ferry business.

network_thesis.how_to_read: Each corridor below runs from a dock Hornblower already operates from or near. LaGuardia is new inventory on a route with no scheduled service today. The two East End legs sit alongside the region's premium air seat, priced below it, and run as an extension of Hornblower's own East Coast operating footprint.
network_thesis.coverage_note: The same fleet proving these four corridors extends across the wider harbor and Long Island Sound as further corridors are mapped, using dock and terminal access Hornblower already holds through NYC Ferry, the Statue/Ellis concession, and City Cruises.

partner_context.their_ambition: You operate the largest public ferry system in the harbor — NYC Ferry, 7.1 million trips in FY2024 across 38 vessels — plus the National Park Service's Statue of Liberty/Ellis Island concession and City Cruises' dining and sightseeing product at Pier 15. Company-wide, City Experiences and Hornblower Group serve more than 20 million guests a year across more than 100 countries and 50 U.S. cities.
partner_context.their_pressure: NYC Ferry operates inside NYCEDC's public subsidy and oversight framework, which structurally limits how a higher-fare, premium product can be priced within that contract. Hornblower completed a Chapter 11 restructuring in July 2024, with Strategic Value Partners now the majority owner and Crestview Partners retaining a minority stake, and is actively electrifying its own conventional hulls — Corvus Energy was selected in December 2024 to supply battery systems for the nine Statue City ferries serving Liberty and Ellis Islands.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier's foiling electric fleet becomes an operator product Hornblower runs directly, using the crews, USCG-compliant marine operations, and dock access it already has across the harbor — a premium tier priced from $50 to $645 a seat, sold and operated separately from the subsidized public-ferry system.

hero.title: City Experiences × Navier — the operator for a foiling premium tier
hero.subtitle: Hornblower runs the harbor's largest public ferry system. Navier brings the foiling vessel technology for a faster, premium product on top of it.
hero.what_we_do_together: We put Navier's foiling electric vessels into revenue service under Hornblower's own marine operating certificate — the same crews, the same USCG-compliant practice, the same harbor. Navier supplies the vessels and the technology; Hornblower supplies the marine operations, terminal access, and the guest base built across NYC Ferry, the Statue/Ellis concession, and City Cruises.

why_now: Hornblower is already running the largest public ferry contract in the harbor and is mid-way through electrifying its own conventional hulls — the December 2024 selection of Corvus Energy battery systems for the nine Statue City ferries serving Liberty and Ellis Islands. A foiling, all-electric vessel is the next step on a path Hornblower has already started, not an unfamiliar technology. At the same time, its public ferry business runs inside NYCEDC's subsidy and oversight framework, which structurally limits how a premium, higher-fare product can be priced within that contract. A Navier-built foiling tier gives Hornblower a distinct, farebox-positive premium product — sold and operated separately from the public system, on the same docks it already holds.

why_navier_now.step_change: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water, cutting the wake, motion and noise that come with a conventional displacement hull — a materially different guest experience from the NYC Ferry or City Cruises boats Hornblower runs today, sold at a price point above the subsidized public fare.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Hornblower already holds dock and terminal access across the harbor — Pier 15 for City Cruises, the Battery and Liberty State Park for the Statue/Ellis concession, and NYC Ferry's citywide landings. A Navier berth pedestal adds to existing terminal footprint rather than requiring a new site.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Hornblower emerged from its 2024 Chapter 11 restructuring in July 2024 under Strategic Value Partners' majority ownership, with a new CEO, Stephen A. Edwards, in place from January 2026. A new premium product line, run under the operating discipline the company already has, fits a moment when the company is actively defining what comes next.

multimodal_fit: Hornblower already runs commuter ferries (NYC Ferry), attraction transportation (the Statue/Ellis concession, and separately Alcatraz and Niagara Falls in its wider portfolio), and premium dining/sightseeing product (City Cruises at Pier 15) from the same harbor. A Navier foiling tier adds a fourth, faster product line onto docks Hornblower already operates from, without requiring a new terminal network.

differentiation.why_navier: A materially faster, smoother ride than any conventional-hull product in Hornblower's current fleet, sold at a premium price outside the NYCEDC public-ferry subsidy framework. Hornblower is also already deep into battery-hybrid retrofits of its own hulls — the nine-ferry Statue City ESS program — so a Navier deployment extends an electrification program already underway rather than starting one from scratch.

proof_points.claim: Hornblower operates NYC Ferry, the region's largest public harbor ferry system.
proof_points.evidence: Hornblower operates NYC Ferry under a competitively procured five-year NYCEDC operating agreement beginning October 1, 2023; the system recorded 7.1 million trips in FY2024, a record, across a 38-vessel fleet.
proof_points.source: NYC Ferry FY24 Annual Report; NYCEDC contract announcement, accessed 2026-07-28

proof_points.claim: Hornblower holds a long-term National Park Service concession for the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island ferries.
proof_points.evidence: NPS selected Statue City Cruises (part of Hornblower Group) for a 10-year ferry concession from Battery, Manhattan and Liberty State Park, Jersey City, beginning March 1, 2024; the two sites recorded 3,722,029 recreational visits in 2024.
proof_points.source: National Park Service, 30 Aug 2023; NPS Park Statistics, updated 29 Jul 2025, accessed 2026-07-28

proof_points.claim: Hornblower's parent company reports scale of over 20 million guests a year.
proof_points.evidence: At its July 2024 restructuring emergence, Hornblower Group stated it serves more than 20 million guests annually in more than 100 countries and 50 U.S. cities — a company-published figure from that announcement, not an independently audited 2026 result.

proof_points.claim: Hornblower is already electrifying its conventional ferry fleet in this harbor.
proof_points.evidence: In December 2024, Corvus Energy was selected to supply energy-storage systems for Statue City Cruises' nine-ferry fleet serving Liberty and Ellis Islands, intended to reduce fuel use and emissions; the company's affiliated Alcatraz City Cruises fleet already runs vessels with Corvus ESS capable of fully electric operation.

proof_points.claim: Hornblower completed its financial restructuring in 2024 and has new leadership in place.
proof_points.evidence: Hornblower filed Chapter 11 on 21 February 2024 and completed restructuring in July 2024, with funds managed by Strategic Value Partners acquiring majority ownership and Crestview Partners retaining a significant minority position; Stephen A. Edwards became CEO effective January 1, 2026, succeeding Mike Flaskey, who moved to a senior-advisor role.
proof_points.source: Davis Polk case summary; Crestview/Hornblower completion announcement, 3 Jul 2024; WorkBoat, 4 Dec 2025, accessed 2026-07-28

objections.concern: Hornblower went through Chapter 11 bankruptcy — is it a stable partner?
objections.response: The restructuring closed in July 2024: funds managed by Strategic Value Partners now hold majority ownership, Crestview Partners retained a significant minority stake, and the company's operating contracts — NYC Ferry, the NPS Statue/Ellis concession — continued through and after the process. A new CEO, Stephen A. Edwards, took over January 2026.

objections.concern: Won't a premium water-taxi tier draw the same subsidy scrutiny as NYC Ferry?
objections.response: NYC Ferry runs inside NYCEDC's public subsidy and oversight framework, under which per-passenger subsidy had already fallen over 30% from its FY20 peak by FY24. A Navier tier is a separate, unsubsidized, premium-priced product sold outside that public contract — farebox revenue only, with no claim on public-ferry funding.

objections.concern: Foiling electric vessels are a new technology for Hornblower's crews.
objections.response: Hornblower is already mid-electrification on conventional hulls — the December 2024 Corvus ESS selection for its nine Statue City ferries, and Alcatraz City Cruises vessels already running on battery ESS. Navier provides vessel-specific training and technical support so crews extend existing battery-operations experience rather than starting from zero.

Fleet structure is a partnership question to work out together — leasing, charter, or joint-ownership models can keep capex off Hornblower's balance sheet while Navier retains the vessel technology and maintenance relationship.

the_ask.navier_brings: The foiling fleet — Pioneer II for the harbor corridors, Quanta-LR hybrid for the East End legs — the vessel technology, and the USCG certification path for passenger service.
the_ask.partner_brings: Marine crews, USCG-compliant operating practice, dock and terminal access across the harbor, and a company-wide guest base of 20M+ a year to market a new premium product into.
the_ask.next_step: Pilot a two-corridor premium water-taxi tier — East 34th Street to LaGuardia, and Pier 11 to Paulus Hook — operated under Hornblower's own marine operating certificate, then extend to the East End (Sag Harbor, Montauk) as phase two.

close.title: The operator the foiling tier needs.
close.body: Hornblower already runs the harbor's largest ferry system and is already electrifying its own hulls. Navier brings the foiling vessel; Hornblower brings the crews, the docks, and the guests to put it into service.

rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 10% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market · leading-operator 25% capture, network-wide

rungs.basis: add food, stays, and experiences to every crossing in the induced market

growth_case.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
growth_case.modal_headline: Floor to prize — every rung traces to grounded demand

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.
